title: Convergence diagnostics
text: plot_diagnostics() arranges four checks look first - R-hat, effective sample size, divergences HMC energy diagnostic - single figure.  R-hat (top left): potential scale reduction factor, one point per parameter. Values close 1 mean chains agree ; anything 1.05 means haven’t converged distribution need iterations (model misspecified). Effective sample size ratio (top right): Neff/NN_{eff}/N, one point per parameter. Low ratios mean chain highly autocorrelated - raw draws contain less independent information count suggests. Divergences (bottom left): transitions sampler abandon numerical integrator became unstable. Even handful can bias posterior estimates region occur. Energy / E-BFMI (bottom right): marginal energy distribution (πE\pi_E) closely track energy transition distribution (πΔE\pi_{\Delta E}); systematic mismatch signals inefficient exploration.
code: plot_diagnostics(x) #> `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`. #> `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`.

what: What to do if something looks wrong
title: Convergence diagnostics
text: High R-hat / low ESS: run iterations (ndraws), chains (chains) R-hat information detect disagreement. Divergences: tighten priors letting sampler explore implausible, poorly-conditioned region (e.g. narrow min_kappa/ max_kappa, min_sigma_count/max_sigma_count bounds, gamma priors switch rates omega_* closer scale actually expect). persist: check priors consistent data (see prior vs posterior plots vignette("Multirates_inference")), consider increasing adapt_delta max_treedepth.

title: Data generation
text: single wild-type “-” cell grows without death. time t_dr random “-” cell acquires driver, multiplies growth rate epistates 1 + s_dr switch rates. tumour sampled (3000 cells) reaches 1 million 3 million cells. cell counts time phylogenetic forest sampled cells:
code: sim = SpatialSimulation("polyclonal", width = 1e4, height = 1e4, save_snapshot = TRUE)  sim$border_growth_model = FALSE sim$history_delta = 0.1  sim$add_mutant(name = "wt",                epigenetic_rates = c("+-" = omega_n, "-+" = omega_p),                growth_rates = c("+" = lambda_n * (1 + s_epi), "-" = lambda_n),                death_rates = c("+" = 0.0, "-" = 0.0))  sim$place_cell("wt-", 5e3, 5e3)  sim$run_up_to_time(t = t_dr)  sim$add_mutant(name = "B",                epigenetic_rates = c("+-" = omega_n_dr, "-+" = omega_p_dr),                growth_rates = c("+" = lambda_n * (1 + s_epi) * (1 + s_dr),                                 "-" = lambda_n * (1 + s_dr)),                death_rates = c("+" = 0.0, "-" = 0.0))  candidates = sim$get_cells() %>% filter(epistate == "-") cell = candidates[sample(x = 1:nrow(candidates), size = 1), ]  sim$mutate_progeny(cell, "B") wtp = sim$var("wt+") wtn = sim$var("wt-") dcp = sim$var("B+") dcn = sim$var("B-")  sim$run_until(wtp + wtn + dcp + dcn > 1e6) t1 = sim$get_clock() sim$sample_cells("Sampling_1", num_of_cells = 3000)  sim$run_until(wtp + wtn + dcp + dcn > 3e6) t2 = sim$get_clock() sim$sample_cells("Sampling_2", num_of_cells = 3000)  forest = sim$get_samples_forest() counts = sim$get_count_history() %>%   mutate(sampling_time_1 = t1, sampling_time_2 = t2)  forest_nodes = forest$get_nodes()

what: From the data to the model input
title: Inference
text: model input built population sizes “-” “+” compartments two sampling times, number mutations driver branch, CCF driver four sorted samples. Population sizes mutation counts perturbed measurement noise. prior driver “+” → “-” switch rate derived data: tables required init_multirates():
code: data("counts") data("muts") data("forest") data("mu")  # The two sampling times. sampling_times = c(   counts$sampling_time_1 %>% unique(),   counts$sampling_time_2 %>% unique() ) t1 = sampling_times[1] t2 = sampling_times[2]  # Fraction of "-" and "+" cells in the two samples. ccf = forest %>% filter(!is.na(sample)) %>% group_by(epistate, sample) %>%   summarize(n = length(cell_id)) %>% group_by(sample) %>% mutate(n = n/sum(n))  # Total population size at the two sampling times... z1 = counts %>% filter(time == t1) %>%   group_by(epistate, mutant) %>% summarize(count = max(count)) %>%   pull(count) %>% unique() %>% sum()  z2 = counts %>% filter(time == t2) %>%   group_by(epistate, mutant) %>% summarize(count = max(count)) %>%   pull(count) %>% unique() %>% sum()  set.seed(31)  # ... measured with lognormal noise. z1 = exp(rnorm(n = 1, mean = log(z1), sd = 0.2)) z2 = exp(rnorm(n = 1, mean = log(z2), sd = 0.2))  zminus = c(z1, z2) * (ccf %>% filter(epistate == "-") %>% pull(n)) zplus = c(z1, z2) * (ccf %>% filter(epistate == "+") %>% pull(n))  # The driver is the first cell of mutant "B": its branch carries the # mutations accumulated from the root to the driver acquisition. driver_id = forest %>% filter(mutant == "B") %>% pull(cell_id) %>% min() driver_branch = PEPI:::get_branch(forest, cell_id = driver_id, stop_id = 0)  m_driver = muts %>% filter(first_cell_id %in% driver_branch) %>% nrow() m_driver = rnbinom(n = 1, mu = m_driver, size = 100)  # Driver CCF in the four sorted samples, from the VAF of the driver # mutations (VAF 1-, VAF 1+, VAF 2-, VAF 2+). ccf_dr = 2 * (muts %>% filter(first_cell_id %in% driver_id) %>%   dplyr::select(Sampling_1_N.VAF, Sampling_1_P.VAF,                 Sampling_2_N.VAF, Sampling_2_P.VAF) %>%   reshape2::melt(id.vars = NULL) %>%   group_by(variable) %>% summarize(v = mean(value)) %>% pull(v)) # Gamma prior on the "+" -> "-" switch rate of the driver, from a plausible # range of values. The growth rate is bounded above by the growth of the # total population (log-linear fit of noisy counts above 1e5 cells) and below # by the growth of the driver "+" cells between the two samples. z = counts %>% group_by(time) %>% summarize(tot = sum(count)) %>%   filter(tot > 1e5)  z$tot = exp(rnorm(n = length(z$tot), mean = log(z$tot), sd = 0.2))  fit = lm(log(tot) ~ time, data = z)  lambda_max = coef(fit)[["time"]] lambda_min = log((zplus[2] * ccf_dr[4]) / (zplus[1] * ccf_dr[2])) / ((1 + 2) * (t2 - t1))  s_max = 2 s_min = 0.1  # ratio of driver "-" and "+" cells at the second sample rho = (zminus[2] * ccf_dr[3]) / (zplus[2] * ccf_dr[4])  omega_max = rho * lambda_min * s_max omega_min = rho * lambda_max * s_min  omega_gamma = PEPI:::fit_gamma_quantiles(omega_min, omega_max, p1 = 0.05, p2 = 0.95) omega_gamma #> $shape #> [1] 2.950961 #>  #> $rate #> [1] 8.491413 tables = list(    population_sizes = tibble(     time = sampling_times,     type = "sampling",     zminus = zminus,     zplus = zplus   ),    # the wild type is the complement of the driver   wt_ccf = tibble(     time = rep(sampling_times, each = 2),     epistate = rep(c("-", "+"), 2),     ccf = 1 - ccf_dr   ),    driver_muts = tibble(     driver_id = "B",     m_driver = m_driver,     ms_driver = -0.8,     sigma_driver = 0.9,     alpha_n_driver = omega_gamma$shape,     beta_n_driver = omega_gamma$rate,     alpha_p_driver = 0.3,     beta_p_driver = 6   ),    driver_ccf = tibble(     driver_id = "B",     time = rep(sampling_times, each = 2),     epistate = rep(c("-", "+"), 2),     ccf = ccf_dr   ) )  x = init_multirates(tables, m_trunk = 0) tables #> $population_sizes #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>    time type       zminus    zplus #>   <dbl> <chr>       <dbl>    <dbl> #> 1  12.4 sampling  397730.  613447. #> 2  13.1 sampling 1030393. 1863969. #>  #> $wt_ccf #> # A tibble: 4 × 3 #>    time epistate   ccf #>   <dbl> <chr>    <dbl> #> 1  12.4 -        0.338 #> 2  12.4 +        0.303 #> 3  13.1 -        0.227 #> 4  13.1 +        0.225 #>  #> $driver_muts #> # A tibble: 1 × 8 #>   driver_id m_driver ms_driver sigma_driver alpha_n_driver beta_n_driver #>   <chr>        <dbl>     <dbl>        <dbl>          <dbl>         <dbl> #> 1 B              424      -0.8          0.9           2.95          8.49 #> # ℹ 2 more variables: alpha_p_driver <dbl>, beta_p_driver <dbl> #>  #> $driver_ccf #> # A tibble: 4 × 4 #>   driver_id  time epistate   ccf #>   <chr>     <dbl> <chr>    <dbl> #> 1 B          12.4 -        0.662 #> 2 B          12.4 +        0.697 #> 3 B          13.1 -        0.773 #> 4 B          13.1 +        0.775

text: One histogram per parameter, prior (transparent) posterior (solid). Growth parameters (`lambda_n`, `s_*`) shown 2, times (`tmrca`, `t_*`) -60 largest sampled `tmrca`, switch rates (`omega_*`) log10 scale. Prior draws growth parameters beyond 99
